Clara (People Ops): Hey everyone — quick Q from an IC: just had a baby, wants to add them to medical + dependent FSA. What's the process and timeline? Do we need a birth certificate or can we do SSN later?
Devon R: congrats! Usually 30 days to add a newborn for immediate coverage. you'll need a birth certificate or hospital record. SSN can come later but add them now and update SSN once received.
Priya S: to add, go to https://redwoodbenefits.example.com -> My dependents -> Add dependent. choose 'life event: birth' and upload docs.
Theo M: also note payroll premium changes start the next pay period after HR processes the change unless you request retro premium adjustment. depends on carrier.
Clara (People Ops): @Devon @Priya good call. Can you confirm what “hospital record” means for docs? some parents only get a temporary record.
Devon R: hospital birth record, discharge paperwork, or a state birth certificate works. if adoption, we need court docs. for temporary docs, upload PDF and put a note in the comments field. benefits team will accept provisional docs then follow up for final bc.
Priya S: FYI for FSA: dependent care FSA rules require dependent to be claimed on your taxes. You add the dependent in portal but we'll also need the dependent's DOB.
Clara (People Ops): Any steps on changing coverage tier (employee -> employee + child) mid-year?
benefits-bot: Auto-reply: Life event change window = 30 days from event date. Coverage effective date = event date unless carrier rules differ. See policy: https://redwoodbenefits.example.com/policy/life-events
Theo M: If you miss 30 days, you can still add later but might be subject to open enrollment only or need to request a special exception from ER.
Devon R: Practical checklist: 1) Add dependent in portal (life event) 2) Upload hospital record or BC 3) Choose new plan/tier if needed 4) Confirm dependent FSA elections 5) Reply to this thread when done and we'll fast-track processing.
Clara (People Ops): What about premiums paid retroactively? is there payroll deduction to catch up?
Priya S: usually payroll will prorate going back to birth; payroll will deduct any retro premium owed over the next 1-2 pay cycles. we notify you via email when processed.
Clara (People Ops): Great — one more: if partner's on a different employer plan, do we need proof of ineligible coverage?
Devon R: yes — if the partner has access to employer coverage and you're trying to enroll them as spouse (not child), carrier may request proof of loss of coverage. for children, that's not required.
Theo M: example email subject to send docs: 
```
Subject: Benefits docs for life event - [Your Name] - Birth [Child NAME] - DOB 2026-05-02
Attachments: hospital_record.pdf
```
Devon R: ping us once uploaded. we'll confirm within 3 business days and notifiy payroll. :thumbsup:
Clara (People Ops): thanks all — i'll DM the parent and paste this thread. leaving a note to update handbook section with clearer examples for temporary docs. :sparkles:
Priya S: happy to draft wording for handbook.
benefits-bot: Reminder scheduled: If life event not completed within 25 days, you will receive an automated reminder.
